title: NATIONAL WATERWAYS DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME
body_text:
Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), an autonomous organization under Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways has developed a Roll on-Roll off (Ro-Ro) terminal at Muktyala in National Waterway (NW)- 4 (Krishna river) to facilitate Ro-Ro movement. IWAI has also constructed and handed over four floating Jetties to Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (APTDC) during the year 2024 to facilitate the tourism activities. Further, the construction of Ro-Ro terminal at Harishchandrapuram in Andhra Pradesh has been awarded.
The details of funds allocated and utilised for development of NW-4 during the last three years are as under:
Financial Year Funds Allocated/utilised (Rs. crore) 2023-24 0.67 2024-25 1.22 2025-26 18.28
The cargo and passenger movement on NW-4 during 2025-26 was 5.71 Million Tonne and 2.34 Million respectively.
The transfer of land of State Irrigation Dept (3.80 acres) at Ibrahimpatnam, NTR District, Andhra Pradesh is under progress for development of Ro-Ro terminal facilities on NW-4. The availability of adequate water depth for safe navigation in Vijayawada–Muktyala stretch depends on the regulated releases from the Pulichintala Dam, resulting in seasonal variation in navigable conditions. Further, the presence of low- level bridges, old navigational locks and encroachments etc, affects the development and navigation on NW-4.
This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Rajya Sabha.

ministry.name: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways informed the Rajya Sabha about development works on National Waterway-4 (Krishna river), including a Ro-Ro terminal built at Muktyala, four floating jetties handed to Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation, and a new Ro-Ro terminal awarded at Harishchandrapuram. Fund allocation for NW-4 rose from Rs 0.67 crore in 2023-24 to Rs 18.28 crore in 2025-26, while cargo movement was 5.71 Million Tonnes and passenger movement 2.34 Million in 2025-26. The reply also flagged challenges such as land transfer delays, seasonal water depth variation due to Pulichintala Dam releases, and low-level bridges, old locks and encroachments hampering navigation.
enrichment.context:
National Waterways are a key part of India's push to develop inland water transport (IWT) as a cheaper, fuel-efficient, and environment-friendly alternative to road and rail for cargo and passenger movement, in line with the National Waterways Act, 2016, which declared 111 waterways as National Waterways. NW-4, spanning stretches of the Krishna and Godavari rivers along with canals in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, is being developed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) for cargo, passenger, and tourism-linked Ro-Ro (roll-on/roll-off) movement, which allows vehicles to be transported directly onto vessels, reducing transshipment time and cost.

The release highlights recurring structural challenges in India's inland waterways development—dependence on dam-regulated water releases for navigable depth, outdated locks, low-level bridges, and encroachments—which are common bottlenecks across several National Waterways and explain why fund utilization and infrastructure progress remain incremental despite policy emphasis under programmes like Jal Marg Vikas Project (mainly for NW-1) and the broader Sagarmala initiative for port-led development. This reflects the gap between ambitious waterway development targets and on-ground implementation constraints involving multiple state agencies (e.g., Irrigation Department land transfers) and inter-departmental coordination.

prelims_questions.question: National Waterway-4 (NW-4), mentioned in context of Ro-Ro terminal development, is primarily associated with which river system?
prelims_questions.explanation: NW-4 comprises stretches of the Krishna and Godavari rivers along with connecting canals in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, as referenced in the release regarding the Krishna river Ro-Ro terminal at Muktyala.

prelims_questions.question: Which organization is responsible for the development and maintenance of National Waterways in India, as mentioned in the release?
prelims_questions.explanation: The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, develops and maintains National Waterways, including NW-4.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the potential of inland waterways in decongesting India's transport infrastructure and reducing logistics costs. Highlight the key challenges in developing National Waterways, with reference to NW-4.

Examine the inter-departmental and inter-state coordination challenges in the development of National Waterways in India, citing examples of land acquisition, water regulation, and encroachment issues.
